segments.t: The context here is very important. SK stock has been up 500% plus in the last year, and so
this is a stock that has moved massively because of the structural changes we've seen
in the memory market, and that is this massive AI boom is causing huge demand
for certain memory chips, in particular high bandwidth memory, DRAM, etc. All of these
going into chips and data centers that are powering this AI boom, and so that has led
to a massive shortage, huge price rises, and that's why you're seeing record
profits at the likes of SK Hynix and at Samsung as well, and so that has really
supported the share price, and I think more recently there's a bit more
volatility as debate swells around the stickiness and how solid this sort
of AI build-out is right now. It's a big debate over that.
And I mean, one of the key reasons for them to go to the US, those high
evaluations, they wanted to get rid of the Korean discount. Is that that entrance
into the Nasdaq, is that going to eliminate that from when you're speaking
to people? Yeah, typically what you're seeing is Asian stocks have had a discount
to their US peers, in particular on the chip side of the equation. Look at
Samsung, look at SK Hynix historically, they have had that discount. I think
with more US buyers coming into the market, that could potentially narrow
the discount at this point. I think what's going to be key for the
market is how structurally different is the memory market now versus
historically. In the past, what you would see is these very extreme sort of
peaks and troughs of demand cycles, where demand would be rising, supply
couldn't keep up, prices would rise, these companies would do very well,
and eventually supply would catch up and then you'd see the price fall.
What's happening now is there is unprecedented demand for memory, and
the question is, is how quickly can supply catch up? Now I've spoken to a
lot of industry execs over the last few years, the most bullish cases are
second half of 2027, where you begin to see that supply catch up. Most
of the thinking that maybe 2028 is where that...
